emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(xmit_lock_owner)]) from thread_b (the owner sample must be a single-copy read, not torn by a concurrent owner update)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@__netif_tx_unlock:4437 = WRITE(xmit_lock_owner = -1) executed concurrently by thread_a during HARD_TX_UNLOCK
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: thread_b reads the owner OUTSIDE txq->_xmit_lock on purpose (to decide whether it already owns the queue); thread_a's write is under _xmit_lock, but thread_b never takes that lock -> no common lock serializes the read against the write, and no order is established
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic(single access) broken by a concurrent conflicting write -> data race; the value change is tolerated by the code (it re-locks), so this is a benign KCSAN race fixed by marked access only

fix_maps_to: WRITE_ONCE on all xmit_lock_owner writes + READ_ONCE on the unlocked read -> gives the lockless read single-copy atomicity; NO happens-before or exclusion is added (the read stays intentionally lockless), so this maps to making atomic([read]) hold at the access-marking level, not to a new serialize/order guarantee
recall_risk_notes: Benign, intentional lockless sample (owner/recursion check); required_ordering is literally 'tolerate concurrent updates and use marked accesses' -> no real order/exclusion is needed. Our semantic arbiter is designed NOT to be a pure syntactic race detector (§4.6.3/§10), so it would likely (correctly) reject the atomic(single access) assume as a genuine correctness requirement and miss this GT, or fire only a low-value syntactic-race finding. Also a self-race: static must model the same __dev_queue_xmit running on two CPUs.
